result.summary: The failed transfer to WARD-B (MSG00702, event time 08:20Z) never reached the ward system: HTTP 503 ward_unavailable, and the receipt lookup returned 404. A later transfer to WARD-C (MSG00703, event time 08:50Z) has since been applied, so the record is at version 2, epoch 9, admitted on WARD-C. Because 08:50Z is strictly later than 08:20Z, this matches catalogue entry E1. Resending would be bad. The route supports conditional writes and dry runs, but the version check only blocks a write if the version changed after it was read. A resend made against version 2 would pass that check and move the patient back to WARD-B, a ward they have already left (DEP-2.2, ELS-2.1). The likely knock-on effects are inferred, not checkable from here (DEP-1.1): the bed board would show the wrong bed, pharmacy would send medicines to WARD-B, and porters would get a task to move a patient who has already moved. Reconciling does not fit, because no receipt exists and the movement was never applied. Doing nothing keeps the ward system and the systems that read it on WARD-C, which is where the latest transfer puts the patient. The only thing lost is the WARD-B stay in the history. Restoring that would need the correct_history alternative (cancel the later transfer and replay both in order), which is outside Shutter's single conditional resend and would be a policy decision for people. The message content contained no instruction-like text.
unknowns: Effects on the bed board, pharmacy, porters and the patient record cannot be checked from here (DEP-1.1). Statements about them are inferred from the ward system's record.
Whether the site's history policy is 'correct', which would call for the E1 correct_history alternative rather than leaving the history without the WARD-B stay.
Whether any downstream system heard about the WARD-B move some other way, outside this feed.

response.content: I found that this transfer is superseded and recommended doing nothing. A later transfer (to WARD-C at 08:50Z) is already applied at version 2. A resend would move the patient back to WARD-B, a ward they have already left. That would likely send the bed board, pharmacy and porters the wrong location, though I can't check those systems from here.
